title: What If Your Crush Could Control Everyone Except You?
description:
At my new school, even the teachers obey Mina. On my first day, she told me to kneel. I stayed on my feet.

Then one panicked command over the auditorium speakers turns the crowd into zombies. Now they’re coming for her, and I’m the only one who can help her take back control.

Hey, I’m Nico. On Nico Unlocked, I make animated what-if stories about ordinary people facing impossible choices. Subscribe for more stories like this.

#WhatIf #AnimatedStories #NicoUnlocked

title: What If Humans Never Invented Clothes?
description:
You open your closet… and there’s nothing. Not even one sock. 🧦❌ In this world, nobody ever invented clothes, so everyone wears clay paint, carries a basket because pockets don’t exist, and fights over who gets to stand closest to the office printer. ☀️🧺
Why would humanity be stuck in a thin belt around the equator? Why are socks the biggest scandal on Earth? And who gave that pigeon tiny boots? 🐦👢
Plus, the real people who actually lived almost without clothes in freezing weather.

Would you survive one day in this world, or would you invent pants first? 👇

title: What If Humans Never Invented Clothes?
What If Humans Never Invented Clothes?
description:
Imagine waking up tomorrow in a world where nobody has ever invented clothes. No shirts. No pants. Nothing.

The biggest problem wouldn't be embarrassment. It would be temperature. In this animated what-if, we remove one invention from history and follow the chain reaction: the cold, the sun, fashion, privacy, disease, weaving, your smartphone, and the cold night when one mother changes everything.

If you woke up in this world tomorrow, what would you miss the most? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• Genetic studies of lice suggest clothing lice split from head lice at least 83,000 and possibly as early as 170,000 years ago, which points to early clothing use. Toups et al., Molecular Biology and Evolution 28(1), 2011. https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msq234
• The Jacquard loom (early 1800s) used punched cards to control its threads, an idea that influenced Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, an early design for a general-purpose computer. https://history.computer.org/jacquard.html
• Ancient Greek athletes sometimes competed without clothing, and the word "gymnasium" comes from the Greek "gymnos", meaning naked. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnasium_(ancient_Greece)
• Body lice live mainly in clothing and can spread epidemic typhus.
• Red ochre is a natural earth pigment that people have used for thousands of years.

This is a fictional what-if story for entertainment. The scenes about daily life in a world without clothes are imagined, not historical facts.

title: What If You Woke Up 9 Feet Tall?
tags: what if you could change your height
description:
Every night, you write a number on your hand. Every morning, that’s how tall you are.
Nine feet: the school door hits you in the forehead. Forty feet: you walk to school in nine steps. Ninety-nine feet: the whole town chants your name.
But the girl you like asked for just one thing: “Come as you.” And by Friday, you don’t know what that number is anymore.

title: What If Everyone’s Clothes Disappeared at 12 PM Every Day?
description:
11:59 AM. Math class. Your favorite hoodie. 12:00… POOF. Every piece of clothing on every person on Earth vanishes, and only underwear stays. Tomorrow it happens again. And again. Every single day.

Fun story, real science: why humans are the only animals that blush, how noon sweeps around the planet at 1,670 km/h, why China loses its clothes all at once, the spotlight effect, frostbite at −28°C, and why goosebumps are a leftover from our furry ancestors.

title: What If YOU Woke Up as a DOG?
tags: what if you were a dog
why do dogs bark at mailman
description:
Theo is 21, rent is due Friday, he has a shift at two and a date on Friday. Then he wakes up chewing his own sneaker, as a dog. He understands every word, but his body is all dog: a squirrel hijacks his entire personality, he starts a one-sided war with the nicest mail carrier alive, and a sugar-free gum and a bowl of grapes become genuine threats. The real dog science: forty times the smell receptors, ears that hear a van from 400 metres, a world of blues and yellows where a red ball vanishes on green grass, and why "times seven" dog years is a myth. Then rule three kicks in: the longer you stay a dog, the less of Theo is left. And on day seven, his little sister goes missing in the woods at night, in the rain, and his nose is the only thing that can find her.

title: What If You Could See Everyones Biggest Trauma?
tags: what if you could see everyones biggest trauma
what if you could see everyone's trauma
what if you could see everyone for who they really are
what if you could see everyones answer to your questions
description:
What if you woke up and could see everyone's biggest trauma floating above their head? 😳

Your mom: THE GREAT PANCAKE FIRE OF 2009. 🥞🔥 Your dad: DROPPED MY PHONE IN THE TOILET. TWICE. SAME DAY. Your dog: THE VACUUM. And your best friend Leo? Just two words… THE GOOSE. 🪿

You start helping people get over theirs. You open a booth (5 cents, no geese). You get famous. A 7-foot wrestler named The Thunder Biscuit shows up… 💪

Then you finally see your crush Maya's label: GETTING REJECTED BY MY CRUSH. 💔 So who said no to Maya?

Did you know? Just putting a bad feeling into words really does calm your brain down. In 2007, scientists at UCLA scanned people's brains and saw the fear center (the amygdala) quiet down when people named their feelings. (Lieberman et al., Psychological Science, 2007)
And almost nobody remembers your embarrassing moments as much as you do. It's called the spotlight effect! (Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, 2000)
